rationale: A wins slightly because it gives the founder sharper proof gates and cleaner beat discipline: "The tension is the whole story: positive adjusted EBITDA and free cash flow, still unprofitable on a net basis, still carrying significant debt" is a real reporter-ready conflict. B has usable material, especially "Peloton is calling itself profitable. Its own numbers disagree," but it also spends a lane on "How Peloton's new CEO manufactured its first profitable quarter in three years," which tries to build an executive profile out of a thin cost-cutting fact. A still needs fact surgery; "Peloton stopped selling bikes" cannot leave the room.
gaps_in_A: "Peloton stopped selling bikes and started renting them" is not in the update and implies Peloton ended sales; the facts only support a nationwide rental expansion.
"$2,000+ upfront purchase" and "The $2,000 bike" import an outside price point, then use it to carry two rental angles.
"changes who buys Peloton" is a plausible consumer-finance direction, but it asserts a customer-mix shift without demographic, signup, or named-customer proof.
"Peloton posts its first profitable quarter" needs tighter wording around adjusted EBITDA/free cash flow versus net loss; A understands the caveat but lets the headline overclaim.
gaps_in_B: "How Peloton's new CEO manufactured its first profitable quarter in three years" centers an executive story the facts do not yet support: no name, tenure, quote, or strategy beyond cost cuts.
"manufactured" is a loaded verb. If B means cost discipline, say that; if it means accounting optics, prove it.
"renting bikes instead of selling them" overstates the model shift; the update says rental expands nationwide, not that sales are being replaced.
"find-journalists" is early as a next step. The set still needs proof-gating and angle selection before anyone starts building a media list.
